hook: The Viennese doctor who explored the unconscious mind and invented psychoanalysis.

pages.x: Sigmund Freud was born in 1856 in Freiberg, in Moravia, now Příbor in the Czech Republic, the eldest of eight children of a Jewish wool merchant and his young wife. The family moved to Vienna when he was four.
As a young scientist he spent weeks in Trieste cutting open some 400 eels, looking for their male organs, which nobody had found. He did not find them either.

He trained as a doctor of the nerves. In 1885 in Paris he watched the famous doctor Charcot treat patients with hypnosis. Back in Vienna, he found that patients often got better when they talked freely about painful memories.
His patients lay on a couch and said whatever came into their minds. Much of the mind, he argued, is unconscious, and hidden wishes and fears from childhood shape what we do.
pages.fx: It gave rise to talking therapy, and to words we all use, such as ego, denial and a Freudian slip.

pages.x: In 1899 he published The Interpretation of Dreams, arguing that dreams are disguised wishes, "the royal road to the unconscious". It sold only 351 copies in six years.

He smoked about 20 cigars a day. He is supposed to have said that "sometimes a cigar is just a cigar", but no one has found that he ever did. The cigars gave him mouth cancer, and he had more than 30 operations.

When Nazi Germany took Austria in 1938, the secret police questioned his daughter Anna. Friends paid for the family to escape to London. Four of his sisters, left behind, were murdered in the Holocaust. He died in London in 1939.
Freud's ideas about the unconscious changed psychology, medicine, art and literature, though many of his theories are now disputed.
pts: Explored the unconscious mind and dreams
